clue.text: 2s attributed to 22:'Milk-calf as seen in velouté, I plead. Oh boy! It revivifies'.

indicators.note: to revivify is to bring back to life in a new form, so the quoted letters are brought back in a fresh order

parts.words: Milk-calf as seen in velouté, I plead. Oh boy! It

explanation.surface: A recipe line praising veal in a creamy velouté sauce as a pick-me-up for a pleading diner.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points at two other answers: 2-down's dying utterances credited to 22-across, the Prime Minister William Pitt the Younger. Bellamy's was the refreshment house at the old Houses of Parliament. The whole quoted phrase up to 'It' is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitt the Younger is said by some to have died asking for one of Bellamy's pies, a famously unheroic farewell utterance.

clue.text: The rage of zythum? Amen to that!

definitions.meaning: the latest fashion, the newest and most up-to-date thing
zythum, an ancient malt drink, is the final entry in Chambers Dictionary, and amen is what closes a prayer: each is the closing word

explanation.walkthrough: Zythum is an obscure word for Egyptian beer, chosen because it sits at the very end of the dictionary.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both the newest fashion and the final utterance that ends a text or argument.

clue.text: Runner on time for take-off

parts.note: a ski is a runner on snow, like a sledge runner

explanation.surface: A sprinter positioned for the start of a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' suggests an athlete, but it is the long blade of a ski; 'on' just places the T after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A take-off is a parody or comic imitation, which is what a short satirical sketch is.

clue.text: See 1
Charles's motto translated from aphoriser, verbally

indicators.note: from signals that the letters are taken out of a run of the following words

explanation.surface: A pithy phrase-maker rendering the Prince's motto into English speech.
explanation.walkthrough: Ich Dien is the German motto under the Prince of Wales's feathers, Charles's title when the puzzle appeared; 'from' takes the run straddling the comma.
explanation.definitionFit: The English rendering of the German motto Ich Dien is a short statement of humble duty.

clue.text: His tales hot from Heinrich or Thomas

parts.note: H is the usual abbreviation for hot, as on taps
off can mean from, as in 'jump off the wall'
Heinrich and Thomas Mann were German novelist brothers

explanation.surface: A story-teller's work fresh from one of two famous German writers.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the title of Offenbach's opera The Tales of Hoffmann, whose hero is the German writer E T A Hoffmann.
explanation.definitionFit: Offenbach's opera The Tales of Hoffmann tells stories belonging to the German Romantic author, so these are his.

clue.text: A wild oriental frenzied festival

indicators.note: frenzied means wildly agitated, so these letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: E for east, the oriental direction

explanation.surface: Someone from the east going wild with excitement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frenzied' rearranges AWILD with E (east, from 'oriental').
explanation.definitionFit: Dewali, more often spelt Diwali, is the Hindu festival of lights held in autumn.

clue.text: Such interference with fig in aperient he dispensed

indicators.note: dispensed as a pharmacist makes up medicine, so the letters are made up anew

explanation.surface: A pharmacist mixing figs into a laxative, which is meddling of a sort.
explanation.walkthrough: An aperient is a laxative, and figs are a traditional one, so the medical picture holds together.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a hand in something that is not your business is the idiom for meddling involvement.

clue.text: Like Lear's child, this one's gone to inhale joints

indicators.note: inhaling takes something inside, so the shortened word swallows the joints
one has gone means a letter standing for one is removed from 'this'

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
ankles are joints of the leg

explanation.surface: A drug-smoking child who has abandoned home.
explanation.walkthrough: Joints and inhaling suggest cannabis, but these are leg joints; 'one' is the Roman numeral I.
explanation.definitionFit: King Lear says a thankless child is sharper than a serpent's tooth, describing his ungrateful daughters.

clue.text: See 1
Wholly involved with the Latvian grandmaster

parts.note: into means keen on or engaged with, as in 'into chess'
Mikhail Tal, the Latvian world chess champion

explanation.surface: Someone completely absorbed in the games of a famous chess player.
explanation.definitionFit: Wholly and in total both mean altogether, completely, an adverbial synonym.

clue.text: Hold the burden

definitions.meaning: to hold back, abstain from doing something
a burden is the chorus or repeated part of a song

explanation.walkthrough: 'Burden' here is the old musical sense of a recurring chorus, not a load.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to abstain from an action and a chorus repeated after each verse.

clue.text: "A thousand times no!" encapsulated in this Reformer

parts.note: K stands for a thousand, as in a salary of 30K
taken as written
X is the multiplication sign, read as times

explanation.surface: An emphatic refusal from a stern Protestant preacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A thousand times no' reads as K × NO; the times sign goes after the two pieces in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: John Knox led the Scottish Reformation in the sixteenth century, a leading Protestant reformer.

clue.text: Command return of musical prime suspect

indicators.note: suspect as an adjective means dubious, so the letters of prime are not to be trusted in their order
a return goes back the way it came, so the show's name is read backwards

parts.note: Evita is the Lloyd Webber musical about Eva Perón

explanation.surface: An order that a show's chief villain should come back on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspect' rearranges PRIME as IMPER; 'return of' turns EVITA into ATIVE. The surface reads 'prime suspect' as a police term.
explanation.definitionFit: An imperative is a command, and in grammar the mood used for giving orders.

clue.text: Fish freezes in volumes

parts.note: the cod is a fish
ices means freezes

explanation.surface: A fish frozen into blocks in large quantities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'volumes' looks like a measure of quantity; it means books.
explanation.definitionFit: Codices are ancient manuscript books, so they are volumes in the bound-book sense.

clue.text: This from Mr Bentley, Biographises intently, As you'd expect from a journo, Unlike some imitators I know

definitions.text: This from Mr Bentley, Biographises intently, As you'd expect from a journo, Unlike some imitators I know

parts.words: This from Mr Bentley, Biographises intently, As you'd expect from a journo, Unlike some imitators I know
parts.note: the clue is itself a comic four-line biographical verse of the type invented by the journalist Edmund Bentley

explanation.walkthrough: Edmund Clerihew Bentley invented this verse form: four irregular lines in two rhyming couplets, usually about a named person. The clue demonstrates it.
explanation.definitionFit: The comic quatrain about a famous person is named from the middle name of its inventor, E C Bentley.

clue.text: Against nature, if one replaces a dud tube

parts.note: V is short for versus, against

indicators.note: a dud is faulty and fails to work, so the altered letters fall into a new order
one is I, the Roman numeral, put where the letter a stands in nature

explanation.surface: A broken pipe that defies the laws of nature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dud' looks like an adjective for the tube, but it signals the anagram; 'one' is the Roman numeral I.
explanation.definitionFit: A venturi is a constricted tube used to measure or speed up fluid flow, named after an Italian physicist.

clue.text: See 1
Sphere of Roman Catholic leaders?

definitions.meaning: a sphere is a whole domain or world, the cosmos

explanation.walkthrough: 'leaders' means editorials, not church heads; The Universe was a long-running Catholic newspaper in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The cosmos is everything that exists, the whole sphere, and also the title of a Catholic weekly.

clue.text: Disloyal? Not US!

definitions.meaning: disloyal to the United States, as the McCarthy-era committee alleged
not of the USA, literally without American character

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes the prefix literally: not American.
explanation.definitionFit: The word was used for those deemed disloyal to America, and literally means not belonging to the USA.

clue.text: It is found in every river

parts.note: all can stand for every, as in 'all men'
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A substance present in every river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' looks like a pronoun but is the old slang for sex appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: It is dated slang for sex appeal or attractiveness, which is what charm or allure means.

clue.text: Divine cowgirl, we hear, passed the salt

parts.note: Io, loved by Zeus, was turned into a heifer: a girl made a cow by a god

indicators.note: we hear means a word is spoken, and its sound written another way

parts.note: passed away, died, whose sound matches the chemical ending

explanation.surface: A ranch girl dying at the dinner table after handing over the seasoning.
explanation.walkthrough: Io, loved by Zeus, was turned into a heifer. The salt's ending is pronounced like the word for passed away, though spelt differently.
explanation.definitionFit: An iodide is a salt of hydriodic acid, such as potassium iodide added to table salt.

clue.text: It's hell, listening to the PM

indicators.note: listening means the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: the pit is hell, the bottomless pit

explanation.surface: A complaint that hearing the Prime Minister speak is torture.
explanation.definitionFit: William Pitt the Younger was British Prime Minister in the late eighteenth century, as was his father.

clue.text: Held on to see daughter hitched

parts.note: allied means joined together, hitched

explanation.surface: Waiting around to watch one's daughter get married.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hitched' suggests marriage, but it means joined, allied.
explanation.definitionFit: To dally is to delay or linger, so dallied means held on or hung about.

clue.text: Charge for rope trick, get back inside!

indicators.note: inside means one piece goes within the other
a trick plays with the letters of rope, setting them out differently
back means the word get is turned round

explanation.surface: A fee for a rope-trick act, and a call to retreat indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charge' is a person in one's care, not a fee, though the surface reads it as payment for a rope trick.
explanation.definitionFit: A protégé is a person in someone's care or charge, a ward or person under patronage.

clue.text: Composer told to depart from Sloane Square!

indicators.note: told means the word is spoken rather than written
a Sloane Ranger accent, from the smart London district, says the word with a long drawn vowel

parts.note: to go off is to depart

explanation.surface: A musician being sent packing from a smart London square.
explanation.walkthrough: Sloane Rangers are posh young Londoners from around Sloane Square; their 'off' sounds like orf. Carl Orff wrote Carmina Burana.
explanation.definitionFit: Carl Orff was the German composer of the choral work Carmina Burana.

clue.text: Emanations of a primitive primate going quietly

parts.note: ur- is a prefix meaning primitive or original

indicators.note: going means a letter leaves the word

parts.note: an ape is a primate
P is piano, the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: An early ape creeping away silently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going quietly' removes P from APE, leaving AE.
explanation.definitionFit: Aurae is a plural of aura, a subtle emanation or atmosphere surrounding something.

clue.text: Roman judgement days satisfied constituents

indicators.note: constituents are component parts, so the letters of satisfied are the parts to be rebuilt

explanation.surface: Voters content with the days when verdicts are delivered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'constituents' suggests voters, but signals the letters of SATISFIED rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Rome the dies fasti were the days on which courts could sit and judgements be given.
